name: VBCI (Vehicule Blinde de Combat d'Infanterie) with the Dragar one-man 25 mm turret

published.source: en.wikipedia 'VBCI' (raw page cached for js/hero/fr_armour2.js): 7.6 x 2.98 x 3 m. The length is not gated: 7.6 m is the hull; the model's 7.86 m X extent runs from the rear stowage box (x -4.05) to the bow (3.80).

engine_contract.current_nodes: one 'turret' group (origin on the ring at the deck, x -0.35 y +0.20 z 2.36; gun along +X) and four 'roadwheel' groups (one per axle, both tyres, origin on the axle, axle along Y)

references.name: [V1] VBCI '6094 0048' OURCQ 1918, dead side-on from starboard
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'VBCI (Vehicule Blinde de Combat de l'Infanterie), French army licence registration '6094 0048', OURCQ 1918, photo-1.JPG', 1280 x 960 (thumb.php width 1280), cached in the scratchpad q_fra2_ref
references.note: THE VBCI TABLE of fr_armour2.js. Long-lens photograph square to the starboard side, nose right, at 137.6 px a metre from the published 7.60 m hull, which makes the tyres 1.26 m (the 14.00 R 20's own size): two figures agree at one scale. X = (px - 662) / 137.6, Z = (819 - py) / 137.6. The outline is hand-traced over the upper hull and the turret only (trees behind: no mask), window_m keeps the tyres and the lower hull out; the gun, the Galix, the bow mirror post and the whip are left out by ignore_m. Read by eye at 2x: about +-0.04 m.

references.name: [V3] VBCI, Metz, 14 July, front left
references.note: For the reviewer: the boat bow with the lamp recesses behind wire mesh, the big mirror on its post at the bow corner, the bolt columns of the add-on armour, the step plates under the chine, the turret left of centre. Camouflage and numbers are not part of the spec.

references.name: [V2] VBCI in the Musee des Blindes, head on
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'VBCI in the Musee des Blindes, France.JPG', 1280 x 961
references.note: For the reviewer: the bow band with the two lamp recesses, the turret left of centre, the upper sides leaning in. No scale taken.

must_show: eight big tyres on four axles at x +2.43, +0.86, -0.97, -2.66, the long gap between the second and third (1.83 m against 1.57 / 1.69 m) [V1]
the boat bow: the glacis from the roof at x 2.09 down to the bow at x 3.80, z 1.80, the lower nose plate raking back to the belly at x 2.90 [V1]
the upper sides vertical from the chine (z 1.52) to z 1.62 and then leaning in to the roof edge (half width 1.49 -> 1.22 at z 2.36) [V1, V2]
the small Dragar turret left of centre (ring at x -0.35, y +0.20), roof at z 3.03, the round sight head at x -0.65..-0.41 up to z 3.53, the 25 mm barrel to x 2.37 [V1, V2]
the add-on armour's bolt columns at about 0.6 m spacing along both upper sides, three bolts high (z 1.66 / 1.95 / 2.24), with the panel joints [V1, V3]
the three small access hatches with handles high on each side at x -3.48, -1.15, +1.15 [V1]
the step plates under the chine at x -0.40..0.47 and 1.27..2.11 [V1]
the bow band with the two lamp recesses behind wire mesh at y +-0.85..1.42, z 1.52..1.68, and the mirror posts at the bow corners (x 2.90) [V2, V3]
the Galix smoke launchers, three tubes at each corner of the rear plate below the roof edge, x -4.10..-3.80, z 1.93..2.30, firing back and out [V1]
plain paint: one coat of green, no camouflage, numbers or roundels; team colour in strips on the roof (x -3.55) and the turret roof (x -1.15)

not_confirmed: the upper sides' lean (roof edge half width 1.22 m) and the bow's narrowing: no head-on drawing with a scale
the turret ring's place (x -0.35, y +0.20 left of centre) and the turret's length: V1 shows the turret body x -1.20..0.42; the model's loft runs x -1.21..0.47
the stowage rack behind the turret roof in V1 (x -1.6..-1.07, z 3.07..3.13): not identified, not drawn
the bolt columns' exact stations, the hatch and step sizes, the mesh bar count, the mirror head size: read by eye or by proportion
the green: the plain-paint policy's one coat (#414e35 authored, with weathering) - the real vehicles of the period wore the Centre-Europe three-tone (V1, V3)
the lower hull is painted the same green; V1 shows it black (part of the three-tone)
